question.text: The Magna Carta was signed by this king, the youngest of five sons of Henry II and Eleanor of Aquitaine.
question.clue: He allegedly murdered his nephew Arthur of Brittany and at the Battle of Mirabeau he rescued his mother Eleanor of Aquitaine.

swap.leadin: Answer the following questions about Brexit.
swap.text: This Conservative prime minister resigned as a result of Brexit. Theresa May succeeded him in July 2016.
swap.clue: In August 2011, this leader controversially proposed that social media might be restricted during riots, such as the ones which swept his capital earlier that month.

question.leadin: Name these British Prime Ministers and one son of a PM who wrote things.
question.text: This Prime Minister is the only to have won the Nobel Prize for Literature. He penned The River War about his adventures as a cavalry man in the Sudan and served as a war correspondent for the Daily Sun during that time. He gave many speeches and led Britain through World War II.
question.clue: This attendant of the Yalta Conference gave the "finest hour" speech.

swap.leadin: Name these Prime Ministers who belonged to the Labour Party of the United Kingdom.
swap.text: This man became the first Labour Party Prime Minister in 1924, but was later kicked out due to his creation of the National Government.
swap.clue: He ended his political career as Lord President of the Council for two years, in political isolation as a result of making a power-sharing pact with the Conservatives four years prior.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Christmas in British history.
question.text: Celebrating Christmas was banned during the rule of this man, who served as Lord Protector after Charles I was executed at the end of the English Civil War.
question.clue: Troops under this man massacred civilians at Wexford and Drogheda while fighting in Ireland.

swap.leadin: Early English monarchs are often forgotten.
swap.text: This only king of England to hold the title of "the Great" was a king of Wessex.
swap.clue: He adopted his former enemy Guthrum and forced his conversion to Christianity.

question.leadin: Name the following about the Midlothian campaign.
question.text: The Midlothian campaign was the brainchild of this politician. This consistent rival of Disraeli led the Liberal Party to victory in the 1880 election, starting the second of his four stints as Prime Minister.
question.clue: His pamphlet on the "Question of the East" opposed Turkish massacres, which he called the "Bulgarian Horrors," and was written during his Midlothian campagin.

swap.leadin: The night before this event began, the Santisima Ferdinand covertly landed at Mullet Creek.
swap.text: Name this brief 1982 war fought over the namesake British archipelago in the South Atlantic Ocean. Military engagements during this war include the Battle of Goose Green and the sinking of the General Belgrano cruiser.
swap.answerHtml: Falklands War (or Falkland Islands War; accept South Atlantic War)
swap.clue: This conflict began when one side's troops landed on April 2, and ended when they were forced to give up the territorial capital of Port Stanley in mid-June of the same year.

question.text: This man defeated Richard III at Bosworth field and took the crown.
question.answerHtml: Henry VII [or Henry, Earl of Richmond; prompt on Henry Tudor]
question.clue: He defeated the pretender Lambert Simnel at the Battle of Stoke Field, and he established the system of Justices of the Peace.

swap.leadin: This monarch's military exploits helped him negotiate the favorable Treaty of Northampton.
swap.text: Identify this monarch and father of David II, who probably murdered rival John "the Red" Comyn.
swap.answerHtml: Robert the Bruce [or Robert VIII de Bruce or Robert I; prompt on “Robert”]
swap.clue: This man was excommunicated by Clement V after his involvement in in the murder of John Comyn, who was nephew to this monarchs predecessor, John Balliol.

question.text: Earlier, King Burgred of Mercia allied with a West Saxon king of this name after Ivar the Boneless invaded England with his Great Heathen Army. A later king of this name was unseated as King of England by Cnut the Great and be known as the "Unready."
question.clue: He married Emma of Normandy and had a defeat of his troops memorialized in poem at the Battle of Maldon.

swap.leadin: A Soviet competitor to this aircraft, the Tupolev Tu-144, retired its passenger flights after less than a year.
swap.text: Name this commercial aircraft developed by the British Aircraft Corporation and Sud Aviation that was used for transatlantic supersonic commercial flights.
swap.clue: This plane developed jointly by Air France and British Airways, which faced airspace restrictions in several countries after residents complained about the excessive noise that it caused.

question.leadin: Answer the following about British scandals of 1963.
question.text: Conservative Prime Minister Harold Macmillan resigned in 1963 amid the fallout from an "affair" when this Secretary of State for War lied about his extramarital relations with 19-year-old model Christine Keeler.
question.clue: In 1960, this man was appointed to the position of Secretary of State for War by Harold Macmillan.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the different things people did in medieval Europe to amuse themselves and kill time.
swap.text: The Old English Bulldog was raised for this blood sport that involved violence between dogs and bulls. Tudor rulers Henry VIII and Elizabeth I enjoyed a popular version of this practice that used bears.

question.text: The three-fold order organisation of Fuller's "Nine Principles" can be traced to the cabalistic infiuence of this man. Fuller wrote The Star in the West as a study of this man's mystical poetry and edited The Equinox with him.
question.answerHtml: Aleister Crowley [also accept Edward Alexander Crowley ]

swap.leadin: The lyrics of this song traditionally played on the Last Night of the Proms state that less fortunate nations "must in their turn to tyrants fall."
swap.text: Name this song with lyrics on how the title location "arose from out the azure main" has inhabitants that "never, never, never shall be slaves." The title action's object is "the waves."

question.leadin: Answer the following about Neolithic Europe and the Proto Indo-Europeans.
question.text: Probably built by Grooved Ware peoples, this Neolithic village by the sea was unearthed by William Watt on the Orkney Islands of Scotland. This settlement is near the Ring of Brodgar, Maeshowe, and the Standing Stones of Stenness.
question.clue: Modern satellite imagery confirms a network of eight houses as part of this site in the Orkney Islands that was revealed when an 1850 storm blew off its grass cover. This "Scottish Pompeii" is the best preserved Neolithic site in Western Europe.

swap.text: Kenneth moved his capital from Dunadd to this site in Perthshire. A stone named for this village is used for the coronation of Scottish monarchs.

question.leadin: In the early 1900s, this British city's Coal Exchange set the price of coal on the world market.
question.text: Name this city that rose to prominence due to its port's status as a terminus of the Glamorganshire Canal and the Taff Vale Railway. This city's docks area is the site of the Senedd Cymru ("SEN-edh KUM-ree") parliament building.
question.clue: This city is traversed by the Rivers Taff and Ely, and is the capital of Wales.

swap.text: The increased activity of poachers following the collapse of the South Sea Bubble inspired this Robert Walpole-supported act, which introduced the death penalty for being found in disguise in a forest.
